Each proposal below is a protocol. It states a hypothesis, what would falsify it, the unit of
analysis, the data source with a call that proved the source reachable, and the analysis in R,
and it is published in that state before any analysis is run.

The order matters and it is deliberate. A protocol written after the result is known is not a
protocol, and a project that criticizes selective reporting cannot itself decide what its
question was once it has seen the answer. Every proposal therefore carries a date and a status,
and a result page will link back to the protocol as it stood.

## Status values

| status | meaning |
|---|---|
| `proposed` | protocol published, not yet reviewed, not yet run |
| `agenda` | a real gap that cannot be run from public data, recorded rather than skipped |
| `reviewed` | independent reviews attached, published whole including disagreement |
| `running` | analysis in progress against the published protocol |
| `reported` | result published with the protocol and the reviews |

## Review

No proposal here has been reviewed. Review is by two models from different providers, each given
the protocol and instructed to refute it, and no study is reviewed by one model alone. The
Codex account's usage limit was exhausted on 2026-09-16 and resets on 2026-09-20, so reviews
begin then rather than running one reviewer now and calling it review.

## How these were chosen

The three runnable proposals share a property that was the selection rule rather than a
coincidence: each turns the field's own instrument on the field. Meta-research measures whether
others share data, cite retracted work, and report inconvenient findings. None of those
questions had been asked about meta-research itself, and each is answerable from data that is
already harvested or openly available.

That rule also kept out the obvious alternative. A study measuring transparency, or FAIRness, in
one more specialty would be a rate in a new population, and rates in new populations are what
this corpus already contains in quantity. Each proposal here has an exposure, an outcome and a
direction, and each can come out the other way.

The fourth entry is not runnable and says so.
